transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I feel like the future has just kind of closed in on me, like there isn’t much to look forward to anymore. My primary care doctor referred me to see you after I talked to her about how I've been feeling. It just feels like I'm stuck.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by feeling like there isn't much to look forward to, and have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

It feels like my future has narrowed down to just grinding out numbers at the bank until retirement, and I keep thinking, "What's the point?" I've completely stopped hiking, going to pottery classes, and tending my garden because of it. Even trying to plan a foliage road trip recently felt like an exhausting chore rather than something to look forward to.
Have you experienced a significant decrease in pleasure from almost all activities, or are there still some things that you find enjoyable, even if it's just a little?

Yes, I really have. The things I used to love like pottery, gardening, or even planning a road trip just feel completely pointless now, or like an exhausting obligation. Even when something genuinely nice happens, like my daughter calling with good news, the feeling just sort of bounces off me without bringing any real joy.
How long have you been feeling this way, and has it been a gradual change or did it start rather suddenly?

It’s been going on steadily for a little over two years now, starting a few months after my bank merged. It was a very gradual change that crept up on me as work became more demanding and transactional, slowly draining my energy until I realized I had given up on all my hobbies.
Can you think of any recent events or times when you felt even a small amount of pleasure or happiness, even if it was fleeting, or has it been completely absent for the past two years?

No, it really feels like it has been completely absent. Even when something objectively good happens, like my daughter calling with nice news or a positive moment at work, the happiness just bounces right off me. It is as if my ability to feel any kind of pleasure has been entirely blocked.

You've mentioned that you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy and can't feel pleasure, but can you tell me if you've also experienced any changes in your appetite or sleep patterns over the past two years?
I haven't really noticed any significant changes in my sleep or my appetite. They've both stayed pretty much the same, even though my energy is so low.
Have you experienced any thoughts of death or suicidal ideation during this time, or have you felt like you're just going through the motions of life without any thoughts of harming yourself?

No, I don't have any thoughts of harming myself or wanting to die. But I absolutely feel like I'm just going through the motions of life, moving through molasses because everything feels so heavy and pointless. It really is like there is just nothing to look forward to anymore.

You've described feeling stuck and a lack of pleasure in activities, but can you tell me if there are any days where your symptoms are significantly worse, or if they've been relatively consistent over the past two years?

They have been very steady and consistent, day in and day out. Since shortly after the bank merger a little over two years ago, this heavy feeling has just been constant without any real ups and downs. It doesn't really come and go in waves; it's just always there.

Have you had any previous episodes like this in your life before the bank merger, or is this the first time you've experienced such a prolonged period of feeling stuck and lacking pleasure in activities?
No, I don't recall ever feeling this way before the merger. This level of prolonged sadness and lack of pleasure is entirely new to me.

Given that you've been feeling this way for over two years, can you think of any periods within that time where you had at least two months without these symptoms, or have they been continuously present?

No, there haven't been any breaks or periods where I felt better at all. It has been completely continuous and steady since it started a little over two years ago, shortly after the merger. I haven't had even a couple of weeks of relief, let alone two months.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been constant for over two years without any significant improvement, but can you confirm if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your feelings of hopelessness or loss of interest, even if they haven't completely disappeared?

No, there really haven't been any variations in how I feel. It has just felt incredibly flat, constant, and steady since this all started over two years ago. I haven't experienced any real ups or downs in that hopelessness or lack of interest at all.
Have you been experiencing any feelings of guilt or worthlessness, or is it more of a neutral, empty feeling that you're describing?

No, I wouldn't say I feel guilty or worthless. It's much more of a heavy, gray, and empty feeling where nothing seems to penetrate or bring me any joy. It just feels very flat, like everything good just bounces right off me.
You mentioned not feeling guilty or worthless, but can you elaborate if there are any specific thoughts or beliefs about yourself that contribute to this feeling of being stuck and empty?

I don't really have any specific negative thoughts or beliefs about myself as a person. It's more of a general sense of hopelessness about the future, where I just feel like nothing is ever going to change or get better.
